stories.headline: Five buildings where the staircase is the facade
stories.claim: Dezeen surveys five public buildings where stairs form the main facade, including Indore's Prestige University and MVRDV's Tirana pyramid.
stories.summary: Dezeen highlights five public buildings where staircases define the facade, from a 460-step university roof in India to a reworked Albanian dictator's monument. Sanjay Puri Architects' Prestige University in Indore has more than 460 stepped platforms, a 9,000-square-metre walkable roof and room for 3,000 students, and was named education project of the year at the 2026 Dezeen Awards. MVRDV has added steps on all sides of the Pyramid of Tirana, built for Enver Hoxha. Other examples are Snøhetta's Shanghai Opera House, Hiroshi Nakamura's Ribbon Chapel in Onomichi and Kengo Kuma's Hisao & Hiroko Taki Plaza in Tokyo. The piece is an architectural feature focused on public access.
key_points: Prestige University in Indore, India, by Sanjay Puri Architects has over 460 stepped platforms and a 9,000 sq m walkable roof.
The university was named education project of the year at the 2026 Dezeen Awards.
MVRDV turned the Pyramid of Tirana, built for Enver Hoxha in the 1980s, into a public space with steps on every side.
Snøhetta's Shanghai Opera House has a spiral staircase that cantilevers from the facade; roof access is now limited to paid ticket holders.
Hiroshi Nakamura's Ribbon Chapel in Onomichi, Japan, has two intertwining staircases meeting at a 15.4-metre viewing platform.
Kengo Kuma's Hisao & Hiroko Taki Plaza at Tokyo Institute of Technology is partly sunken with an external stair mirrored inside.

It is the studio's first finished project in Africa and sits between Rabat and Salé near the Mohammed VI Tower. stories.headline: Will Anthropic buck the tech sell-off?
stories.claim: A sharp AI-led sell-off pushed the S&P 500 into a correction and the Nasdaq into negative territory for 2026.
stories.summary: US stocks suffered a bruising AI-led sell-off on Friday, with the S&P 500 falling 3.7% to its worst weekly loss in more than 18 months and entering a correction, more than 10% below its 6 October all-time high. The Nasdaq Composite slumped 5.3%, pushing it into negative territory for the year, while the Dow fell 1.9%. Chipmakers Nvidia, Micron, Broadcom and AMD bore the brunt, and Anthropic shares tumbled 8.5% a day after its successful IPO. The rout spread abroad, with Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's Kospi each falling more than 5%. Investors fear AI spending and valuations are unjustified, and election results favouring curbs on data centre construction have added to bubble worries.

Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's Kospi each fell more than 5% overnight, and European indexes also fell sharply.

stories.headline: New ‘Planet X’ Theory Suggests Something Big Is Hiding Beyond Neptune
stories.claim: A new study proposes a possible 'Planet X2' of 1.5 to 2 Earth masses beyond Neptune to explain distant icy object orbits.
stories.summary: A new study in the Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society proposes that an undiscovered planet, dubbed Planet X2, could be orbiting far beyond Neptune, with between 1.5 and two times Earth's mass. The research, led by Patryk Sofia Lykawka, used computer simulations over about 4.5 billion years of solar system history. The hypothetical world would sit at 350 to 500 astronomical units on a highly elongated orbit, never coming closer than 200 AU to the Sun, compared with Neptune's roughly 30 AU. The model aims to explain odd orbits of distant bodies such as Sedna. It is separate from the better-known Planet Nine hypothesis, which posits a body of about 6.2 Earth masses.
key_points: The study was published in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society and led by Patryk Sofia Lykawka.
Planet X2 is proposed to have between 1.5 and two times Earth's mass.
Simulations tested orbits with a semi-major axis of 350 to 500 AU, staying at least 200 AU from the Sun.
The model reproduced several observed patterns among distant objects, though differences with observations remain.
The idea is distinct from Planet Nine, which is modelled at about 6.2 Earth masses and 380 AU.
No observational detection of the planet has been reported.
